claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Controlled porosity can be introduced into HfMoTaTiZr through powder metallurgy.
Introducing porosity will reduce the bulk density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Optimizing pore size and distribution can preserve the mechanical properties of porous HfMoTaTiZr.
Controlled porosity can reduce density without significant loss of mechanical strength.
The proposed strength retention applies from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposed performance applies under both tensile and compressive loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, while the falsification rule permits strength losses of up to 10%. The predicted outcome instead uses the weaker phrase 'without significant loss,' leaving the accepted degree of sacrifice inconsistent across fields.
